criteria.criterion: `athena --version` output is built from wiring::build_info() and includes the package version and the source commit (short or full hash); clap's default CARGO_PKG_VERSION-only version string is replaced.
criteria.evidence: main.rs drops the bare `version` attribute and builds the command with `Cli::command().version(wiring::version_string(&wiring::build_info()))`. version_string formats `{version} (commit {source_commit}[, dirty])`.

criteria.criterion: A build with no embedded commit, or with ATHENA_BUILD_DIRTY not 'false', is shown as such (e.g. 'unknown' and/or 'dirty'), consistent with build_info()'s dirty rule.
criteria.evidence: version_string prints `build.source_commit`, which build_info() sets to 'unknown' when no commit is embedded, and adds ', dirty' whenever `build.dirty` is true. That flag comes from the existing rule: no commit, or ATHENA_BUILD_DIRTY != Some("false") (wiring.rs:30).

criteria.criterion: A unit or integration test covers the version-string formatting for clean, dirty, and unknown-commit builds.
criteria.evidence: tests/version.rs has clean_build_names_its_commit, dirty_build_is_marked and unknown_commit_is_marked_dirty, plus binary_prints_the_build_info, which runs the real binary. All 4 passed.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo run -p athena-cli -- --version` (no build env set): it exits 0 and prints the version with an 'unknown' commit marked as dirty/unknown.
criteria.evidence: Printed `athena 0.1.0 (commit unknown, dirty)`. The command reported no error, which means exit 0, and the binary test also asserts `status.success()`.
Athena's checks on this tree passed: fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, and cargo test --locked (170 tests). I re-ran the new test file and it passed.

findings.summary: The version string is leaked with Box::leak to get a 'static str.
findings.evidence: `Box::leak(wiring::version_string(...).into_boxed_str())` runs once per process, so the leak is harmless. clap's `version` also accepts owned strings through `Str`/`IntoResettable` with the `string` feature, which would avoid it.

findings.summary: The README example shows a shortened hash, but xtask embeds the full `git rev-parse HEAD` hash.
findings.evidence: The example reads `commit 0123abc…`. The ellipsis marks it as shortened, so it is not wrong, but the real output has 40 hex characters (xtask/src/main.rs:233).

summary: The change does what you asked: `athena --version` now shows which commit the binary was built from. I ran it with no build settings and it printed `athena 0.1.0 (commit unknown, dirty)`. The text is built from the existing build_info(), so a binary installed through xtask will show the full commit hash, plus `dirty` when the source had uncommitted changes. New tests check the clean, dirty and unknown-commit formats and also run the real binary; I re-ran them and all 4 passed. `--help` and subcommand parsing still work. Athena's format, lint and test checks passed on this tree. There is no build.rs and no new dependency. All five criteria are met. My only findings are two small nits: the version text is deliberately leaked to give it a static lifetime, which is harmless, and the README example shows a shortened hash while real builds show the full 40-character hash.
